segmentation.text: No motorcycle or motor scooter
shall be ridden upon any sidewalk
of the City

elements.justification: 'motorcycle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, excluding an electric bicycle, a tractor or a moped'), claimed as one atom and never expanded. 'motor scooter' has no applicable definition and the table admits no aggregate for it, so its ordinary words, a scooter propelled by a motor, are carried by the class atoms whose contracts denote such machines: ru.moped ('a low-power two- or three-wheeler with a small engine or motor', the class whose corpus definition names a 'motor-driven scooter') and ru.electric_scooter ('a standing or seated electric scooter with handlebars'); a motor scooter above the moped class is a motor vehicle on not more than three wheels with a seat, so already a member of the motorcycle aggregate. ru.pedestrian is not read: its contract is 'Not a stand-in for: a person on a bicycle or scooter'. 'No' states the prohibition the obligation span carries.

st.sidewalk is the 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line', the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-240 ('that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians'); its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk' is kept: a crosswalk is not read as a sidewalk. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors 'upon' to the subject's own sidewalk, and 'any' makes every sidewalk region count. 'be ridden' is the machine's controlled motion, drv.motion.moving (speed above the source's resolution), under the agency reading disclosed below.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as declared for the map or the trace.

applicability: x is a motorcycle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle), a moped (ru.moped) or an electric scooter (ru.electric_scooter), and asm.within_city_limits holds at the observation.
obligation: At the observation, x is not both moving (drv.motion.moving(x) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution) and occupying (rel.occupies) any st.sidewalk region.

narrowings.why: 'be ridden' is read through the machine's controlled motion: a motorcycle or scooter moving above the speed resolution while its footprint overlaps a sidewalk is taken to be ridden there, one standing still is not; who or what is at the controls is not observed.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Inside declared city limits, a motorcycle travels along a sidewalk at walking pace; its footprint overlaps the sidewalk region and its speed is well above the resolution.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Inside declared city limits, a motorcycle travels in a lane of the roadway, overlapping no sidewalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle is ridden along a sidewalk inside declared city limits; it is neither in the motorcycle aggregate nor a moped nor an electric scooter.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Inside declared city limits, a moped moves near the curb; the source declares rel.occupies absent, so whether it is on the sidewalk is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Inside declared city limits, a motorcycle stands parked on a sidewalk with zero speed: it is not ridden there.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: Ground-truth simulator kinematics sampled at 20 Hz and the speed noise of typical odometry

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to the operation of
vehicles
within a roundabout
All vehicular travel shall be in a counterclockwise direction

elements.justification: 'vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions), claimed as one atom.

st.roundabout is 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches', which denotes DEF-LVMC-11-02-130 ('an intersection characterized by a circulatory roadway, channelized approaches and yield control of entering traffic', encompassing 'the area bounded by the outermost curb line' and including 'the crosswalks on any entering or exiting roadway': the entry and exit approaches the contract names). rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors 'within' to the roundabout the vehicle is in.

'vehicular travel' is the motion of the vehicle the subject span binds (the same aggregate). 'in a counterclockwise direction' is the sense of that motion about the roundabout: drv.motion.clockwise_about_region reads the vector from the region's reference point (st.region_geometry, 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame') to the vehicle's position (kin.position) against its velocity (kin.velocity, 'velocity vector', world frame) and speed (kin.speed); its own exclusion makes it no stand-in for travel against a lane direction, so no lane marking or st.lane_direction is read. The duty is violated by clockwise motion; motion toward or away from the centre (entering, leaving) and standstill are neither sense and do not violate it.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and occupies (rel.occupies) some st.roundabout region at the observation.
obligation: For every st.roundabout region r that x occupies at the observation, x is not moving clockwise about r: not drv.motion.clockwise_about_region(x, r) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution and sine_tolerance p.circulation_sine_tolerance.

narrowings.why: 'counterclockwise' is read as the sense of the vehicle's motion about the roundabout region's reference point (st.region_geometry), taken as the centre its circulatory roadway runs around, viewed from above; the duty is judged by the absence of the opposite (clockwise) sense, so a vehicle at rest or moving radially within the tolerance (entering or leaving) complies.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car on the circulatory roadway of a roundabout drives around the central island clockwise, its velocity tangential to the island.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car on the circulatory roadway drives around the central island counter-clockwise.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives clockwise around a block on ordinary streets; it occupies no roundabout region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is on the circulatory roadway of a roundabout and moving; the source declares kin.velocity absent, so the sense of its motion is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car on an entry approach inside the roundabout's outline drives straight toward the central island before yielding: its motion is radial, neither sense.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: Ground-truth simulator kinematics sampled at 20 Hz and the speed noise of typical odometry

param_proposals.name: p.circulation_sine_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Direction tolerance: the sine of the largest angle off a radial line within which motion about a point counts as neither sense of rotation, covering heading and position noise on entry and exit paths.
param_proposals.source: Measurement tolerance of velocity direction in ground-truth simulation

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
Shall not back into an intersection, on or over a crosswalk, or around a
street
corner

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'driver' is no aggregate: DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle' names a relational role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below), so the duty binds the vehicle's conduct.

Three alternatives of one prohibition. (1) 'back into an intersection': st.intersection is 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection', which denotes DEF-NRS-484A-105 (1) 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines' and (3) 'The junction of an alley with a street, road or highway shall not constitute an intersection'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk or a stop line' is kept: entry into the intersection region itself is read. 'back' is drv.motion.reversing (velocity along heading below minus the resolution, never kin.gear, which is 'Not a stand-in for: the direction of motion'). 'into' is the observation at which x's footprint begins to overlap the intersection (rel.occupies rising) while reversing. (2) 'on or over a crosswalk': st.crosswalk is the 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', which denotes both limbs of DEF-NRS-484A-065 ('That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks' and 'Any portion of a highway at an intersection or elsewhere distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing'). 'on or over' is x's footprint overlapping the crosswalk (rel.occupies) at an observation at which x is reversing (drv.motion.reversing): on it, or passing over it. (3) 'around a' corner, said of backing, is reversing (drv.motion.reversing, from kin.velocity and kin.heading) while the heading changes (drv.motion.yawing, the absolute kin.yaw_rate above the resolution: 'rate of change of heading'); kin.yaw_rate's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature' is respected: the vehicle's own heading change is read, not the road's shape.

A street corner is the corner where ways meet: read as the st.intersection region ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'), whose corners are where the curb lines prolonged by DEF-NRS-484A-105 meet; rel.occupies anchors the backing vehicle to it. The highway part of DEF-NRS-484A-265 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every highway ... open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic') is the ways the intersection lies on; its city part is carried by the assumption on 'street'.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as declared for the map or the trace.

obligation: At the observation none of the following holds: (a) x is reversing (drv.motion.reversing(x), speed_floor p.speed_resolution) and its footprint begins here to overlap (rel.occupies rising) some st.intersection region; (b) x is reversing and occupies (rel.occupies) some st.crosswalk region; (c) asm.within_city_limits holds, x is reversing and yawing (drv.motion.yawing(x), yaw_floor p.yaw_rate_resolution), and x occupies some st.intersection region.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'around a' street corner is read as reversing while the heading changes (drv.motion.yawing); the street corner is read as the intersection region whose corner the vehicle backs around: backing around it is reversing with the heading changing while the footprint overlaps an intersection; the curb corner outside the intersection outline is not a mapped region and is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car reverses along a street and its rear footprint begins to overlap the intersection region at the end of the block.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car reverses into a parking bay mid-block, overlapping no intersection and no crosswalk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle, a device moved by human power and so no vehicle, is walked backwards across a crosswalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint overlaps a crosswalk; the source declares kin.velocity absent, so whether it is reversing is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car stopped past the stop line reverses so that its footprint overlaps the marked crosswalk behind it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Inside declared city limits, a car already within an intersection reverses while its heading swings to the side, backing around the corner into the cross street.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: Outside declared city limits, a car already within an intersection and clear of every crosswalk reverses while its heading swings: no street corner is involved and no entry into the intersection occurs.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: Ground-truth simulator kinematics sampled at 20 Hz and the speed noise of typical odometry

param_proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest yaw rate the acquisition standard separates from a straight path; a yaw rate at or below it counts as no heading change.

segmentation.text: Motor vehicles being driven
upon any highway
outside of a business district
in a caravan or motorcade
whether or not towing other vehicles
shall be operated to allow sufficient space between each such vehicle or combination of vehicles
so as to enable any other vehicle or combination of vehicles to enter and occupy such space without danger

elements.justification: 'Motor vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'), claimed as one atom. 'being driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below).

st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', which denotes DEF-NRS-484A-095 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority when any part of the way is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular traffic'); its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' is respected: the whole way is read. rel.occupies anchors 'upon' to the highway the vehicle is on.

Nearest atoms only (gap below): membership of a caravan or motorcade, an organized group of vehicles proceeding together, has no atom. rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ('a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') and rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') relate the subject to the motor vehicle ahead of it, but they hold for any two vehicles following each other in a lane, members of a group or not, so they do not tell a caravan from ordinary traffic.

'shall be operated to allow ... space between each such vehicle or combination of vehicles' is the vehicle's conduct of keeping a gap to the caravan vehicle ahead of it in its lane: rel.surface_gap ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies'; its longitudinal component along the subject's heading) to the road user that rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ('a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane') places ahead and rel.same_direction ('headings aligned') shows travelling the same way. 'each such vehicle' is a vehicle of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle and 'combination of vehicles' the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles ('two or more vehicles coupled together'), each claimed as one atom: the gap is measured from the body of the vehicle or combination ahead. 'sufficient' is bounded by the standard span's operationalization. 'operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below).

operationalizations.standard: sufficient space ... so as to enable any other vehicle or combination of vehicles to enter and occupy such space without danger
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance for a vehicle merging into a column: the space between consecutive caravan vehicles must hold the longest combination of vehicles that may enter (a design-vehicle length) plus a time headway at the subject's current speed to the caravan vehicle ahead of the entering one and the same headway from the subject behind it; the bound rises with the subject's speed (kin.speed). 'each such vehicle or combination of vehicles' is the caravan vehicle ahead of the subject, a vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) or a combination (DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles, 'two or more vehicles coupled together'), in the subject's lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) and direction (rel.same_direction).

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies outside every business district declared for the map or the trace.

residues.why: The duty is the same for a caravan vehicle that tows another vehicle and for one that does not: the words say so ('whether or not'); a towing vehicle and what it tows form a combination of vehicles, whose gap to the vehicle ahead is read from the combination's body through the aggregate the standard names.

applicability: x is a motor vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle) occupying (rel.occupies) a st.highway region, asm.outside_business_district holds, and x travels in a caravan or motorcade (gap ru.procession_member; nearest reading: some other motor vehicle of the same group travels in x's lane ahead of x (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) and in x's direction (rel.same_direction, tolerance p.same_direction_cosine)).
obligation: For every road user y other than x that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) or a combination of vehicles (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles), belongs to x's caravan, is ahead of x in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) and travels in x's direction (rel.same_direction, p.same_direction_cosine): the longitudinal component of rel.surface_gap between x and y is at least p.entering_combination_length plus p.entry_time_headway times x's speed (kin.speed) for the gap ahead of the entering vehicle plus p.entry_time_headway times x's speed for the gap behind it.

narrowings.why: 'being driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a motor vehicle moving on the highway is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.
'operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the gap the vehicle keeps is its conduct, whoever or whatever controls it.

'without danger' is read only through the length of the longest combination that may enter and a time headway at the subject's speed on each side of it; other factors of danger (weather, grade, sight distance, the entering vehicle's speed) are not read, and 'any other vehicle or combination of vehicles' is read through that one design length.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a rural highway declared outside every business district, three cars travel as a funeral motorcade in one lane at highway speed; the second car keeps a longitudinal gap to the first shorter than the length of an entering tractor-trailer combination.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same motorcade, each follower keeping a gap to the car ahead longer than an entering combination plus a time headway at its speed on each side.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The same tightly spaced motorcade travels through a place declared a business district.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The rural motorcade as in forbid; the source declares rel.surface_gap absent, so the gap the follower keeps is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The lead car of a rural motorcade has no vehicle of any kind ahead of it in the scene: there is no space for it to keep, and it binds alone.

param_proposals.name: p.entering_combination_length
param_proposals.convention: Design-vehicle length: the overall length of the longest combination of vehicles a highway is designed to carry, standing for 'any other vehicle or combination of vehicles' that may enter the space.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book design vehicles (WB-67 interstate semitrailer, 73.5 ft)

param_proposals.name: p.entry_time_headway
param_proposals.convention: Safe time headway: the time gap kept to the vehicle ahead, applied once ahead of and once behind the entering vehicle at the subject's speed.
param_proposals.source: Two-second following rule of driver manuals and headway-based car-following conventions

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine
param_proposals.convention: Heading alignment tolerance: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings that still counts as travelling the same way.
param_proposals.source: Measurement tolerance of heading in ground-truth simulation and lane-keeping heading variation

gaps.proposal: `ru.procession_member` | a road user travelling as a member of an organized group of vehicles proceeding together in a column (a caravan, motorcade, convoy or procession), as the source labels the group; **group** attribute identifying the group, so that two road users are members of the same one **Not a stand-in for:** vehicles that merely follow one another in the same lane | general

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
shall not overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
when such movement requires driving off the paved portion of the highway

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom. 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080, 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below).

'another vehicle' is a road user of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle other than the subject, quantified because it is present only sometimes. 'overtake and pass ... upon the right' is drv.interaction.passing_on_right(x, y): headings aligned (rel.same_direction), bodies side by side along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'), y on x's left (rel.bearing, 'for "on the right of"'), x faster than y (kin.speed). rel.longitudinal_overlap is 'neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies' and is read only as side-by-side.

The paved portion of the highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095, 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way') is told from the unpaved by the paved attributes the ontology carries: st.shoulder 'the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic; paved attribute' and st.road_edge 'curb or edge of the roadway; paved attribute for the surface beyond it'. 'driving off the paved portion' is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a shoulder whose paved attribute is false, or a road edge whose surface beyond is unpaved. 'such movement requires' is read by the movement as made: the pass that is made with the vehicle off the pavement at the same observation is the one the words name.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and, at the observation, x is off the paved portion of the highway: it occupies (rel.occupies) a st.shoulder region whose paved attribute is false, or a st.road_edge whose paved attribute (the surface beyond it) is false.
obligation: At the observation there is no road user y other than x that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and that x is passing on y's right: not drv.interaction.passing_on_right(x, y) with aligned_cosine p.same_direction_cosine and speed_margin p.overtaking_speed_margin.

narrowings.why: 'The driver of a vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, and the duty binds that vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.

'overtake and pass' is judged at the side-by-side phase of the movement (drv.interaction.passing_on_right): an approach from behind on the unpaved surface that never comes alongside, and the return ahead of the other vehicle after the bodies no longer overlap, are not judged by this node.
'driving' off the pavement is read through the vehicle's controlled motion over the unpaved surface, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a two-lane highway a car moves onto the unpaved shoulder and drives alongside a slower car that waits to turn left, the slower car on its left, the bodies side by side.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car alone in the scene pulls onto the unpaved shoulder and slows to a stop: it passes no vehicle, and the duty binds it alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: On a highway with two lanes in its direction, a car passes a slower car on its right within the paved right lane, never leaving the pavement.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car on the unpaved shoulder moves faster than a car beside it; the source declares rel.bearing absent, so on which side of it the other car lies is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car crawling on the unpaved shoulder is overtaken by a faster car in the lane on its left: the subject is slower and passes no one.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cosine
param_proposals.convention: Heading alignment tolerance: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings that still counts as travelling the same way.
param_proposals.source: Measurement tolerance of heading in ground-truth simulation and lane-keeping heading variation

param_proposals.name: p.overtaking_speed_margin
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution of a speed difference: the smallest excess of the subject's speed over the other's that counts as gaining on it rather than keeping pace.
param_proposals.source: Speed noise of ground-truth simulator kinematics, doubled for a difference of two readings

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide
a single right lane to be used only for turning
a vehicle must
Be driven in the right turn lane only for the purpose of making a right turn

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', denoting DEF-NRS-484A-095 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority ...'); st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, ...') ties the turn lane to that highway. 'has been designed to provide' is the lane's presence on the map (status reading below).

st.turn_lane is 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', with side right: 'a ... right lane to be used only for turning'. 'single' is read as no neighbouring lane being a right turn lane too: st.lane_adjacency gives the 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction' (its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes' is respected: lanes, not markings, are compared), so a pair of adjacent right turn lanes is not a single one.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'must' introduces the duty the obligation spans state.

'the right turn lane' is the lane L the condition singles out (st.turn_lane, side right); 'driven in' it is x's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). Driving in it other than for the turn shows where x leaves it into the neighbouring lane on its left (st.lane_adjacency, 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction') short of the intersection it enters (st.intersection), instead of turning. The right turn the lane serves is made at the intersection L runs into: st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), an st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet', DEF-NRS-484A-105). 'making a right turn' is read by the heading change of x since its footprint began to overlap that intersection (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, integrated from kin.yaw_rate, left positive) reaching minus the turn recognition angle by the time x leaves it; kin.yaw_rate is 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature', and the quantity is compared at the exit, after the whole passage. 'the purpose of' is read through the conduct it explains (reading below).

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and x occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation, or occupied at an earlier observation, a single right turn lane L: an st.turn_lane region of side right lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region, with no lane adjacent to it (st.lane_adjacency) that is also an st.turn_lane of side right.
obligation: Re-binding L with the same selection and I as the st.intersection region L enters (st.lane_enters): at the observation neither (a) x stops here occupying L (rel.occupies of x and L false here and true at the previous observation) while occupying the lane adjacent to L on its left (st.lane_adjacency) and not occupying I; nor (b) x stops here occupying I, having begun to overlap I at an observation at which it occupied L, and its heading change since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, I), step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is greater than minus p.turn_recognition_angle: it left the intersection without turning right.

narrowings.why: 'has been designed to provide' is read through the lane's presence as mapped: a right turn lane on the highway evidences the design.
'Be driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion in the lane, whoever or whatever controls it.

'only for the purpose of making a right turn' is read through the conduct the purpose explains: a vehicle in the lane leaves it either by turning right (into the intersection the lane enters, with a right turn, or off to the right before it); leaving it back into the neighbouring lane on its left short of the intersection, or leaving the intersection it entered from the lane without a right turn, is the lane used for another purpose.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the single right turn lane to pass a queue of through traffic, then moves back into the through lane on its left before reaching the intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car drives in the single right turn lane, enters the intersection the lane runs into and turns a quarter turn to the right before leaving it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car approaches an intersection on a highway whose approach has no right turn lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the intersection from the single right turn lane and leaves it; the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent, so whether it turned right is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car changes back out of the rightmost of two adjacent right turn lanes: the highway provides a dual, not a single, right turn lane.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car in the single right turn lane drives straight through the intersection and leaves it with its heading unchanged.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: Intersection geometry conventions (AASHTO Green Book turning paths) and manoeuvre classification in trajectory datasets

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide
a single right lane to be used only for turning
a vehicle must
While being driven in the right turn lane
not travel through an intersection

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines', denoting DEF-NRS-484A-095 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority ...'); st.on_way ('the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, ...') ties the turn lane to that highway. 'has been designed to provide' is the lane's presence on the map (status reading below).

st.turn_lane is 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', with side right: 'a ... right lane to be used only for turning'. 'single' is read as no neighbouring lane being a right turn lane too: st.lane_adjacency gives the 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction' (its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the marking between two lanes' is respected: lanes, not markings, are compared), so a pair of adjacent right turn lanes is not a single one.
'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'must' introduces the duty the obligation span states.

'the right turn lane' is the lane L the condition singles out (st.turn_lane, side right); 'being driven in' it is x's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies), read at the observation at which x's footprint begins to overlap the intersection: the moment the travel through begins.

'an intersection' is the st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', DEF-NRS-484A-105) the turn lane runs into (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'); a turn lane reaches no other. 'travel through' it is entering it from the lane and leaving it (rel.occupies rising, then falling) without the heading change of a right turn: drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry (from kin.yaw_rate, left positive; 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature' is respected, the vehicle's own heading change over the passage is read) not reaching minus the turn recognition angle by the exit.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and x occupies (rel.occupies) at the observation, or occupied at an earlier observation, a single right turn lane L: an st.turn_lane region of side right lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region, with no lane adjacent to it (st.lane_adjacency) that is also an st.turn_lane of side right.
obligation: Re-binding L with the same selection and I as the st.intersection region L enters (st.lane_enters): at the observation it is not the case that x stops here occupying I (rel.occupies of x and I false here and true at the previous observation), having begun to overlap I at an observation at which it occupied L, with its heading change since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(x, I), step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) greater than minus p.turn_recognition_angle.

narrowings.why: 'has been designed to provide' is read through the lane's presence as mapped: a right turn lane on the highway evidences the design.
'being driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion in the lane, whoever or whatever controls it.

'travel through an intersection' is read as entering the intersection from the turn lane and leaving it without turning right: a straight passage and a left turn alike; a passage still under way when the recording ends is not decided.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car in the single right turn lane enters the intersection the lane runs into and drives straight across it, leaving with its heading unchanged.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car in the single right turn lane enters the intersection and turns a quarter turn to the right before leaving it.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives straight through an intersection from a through lane on a highway whose approach has no right turn lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car enters the intersection from the single right turn lane and leaves it; the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent, so whether it turned right is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car in the single right turn lane moves back into the through lane on its left before the intersection and later crosses the intersection from the through lane: it never entered the intersection from the turn lane.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
param_proposals.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
param_proposals.source: Intersection geometry conventions (AASHTO Green Book turning paths) and manoeuvre classification in trajectory datasets

segmentation.text: Every vehicle driven
upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and
must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection
established by a public authority

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below).

A divided highway is 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section' (DEF-NRS-484A-070): an st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which (st.on_way) an st.median_or_divider lies ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'), its parts being st.roadway regions ('separate roadways of a divided highway are separate'). 'upon' is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a roadway or dividing section lying on that highway; st.highway's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' is respected: the roadway is read as the part of the way it is.

The roadways of a divided highway each carry one direction; st.lane_direction is the 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — ... a roadway, one-way roadway'. The right-hand roadway, under right-hand traffic, is the one whose designated direction is the vehicle's direction of travel, so being driven upon another roadway of the highway is moving against the designated direction of the roadway x occupies: drv.motion.against_carrier_direction(x, r), from kin.velocity and kin.speed. The concept is 'Not a stand-in for' the heading opposing the carrier, so a vehicle crossing a roadway at a wide angle is not driven upon it against its direction.

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and occupies (rel.occupies) an st.roadway or st.median_or_divider region lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region h on which some st.median_or_divider region lies.
obligation: Re-binding h with the same selection: for every st.roadway region r lying on h that x occupies at the observation, x does not move against r's designated direction: not drv.motion.against_carrier_direction(x, r) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution and opposed_cosine p.opposed_direction_cosine.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the highway is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

'the right-hand roadway' is read as the roadway whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) is the vehicle's direction of travel, as right-hand traffic makes it; 'only upon' is read as the choice between the highway's roadways, so this node judges travel against a roadway's direction; driving over or within the dividing section is the second obligation of the line, and crossing a roadway at a wider angle than the tolerance is not driving upon it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a highway divided by a raised median, a car drives along the roadway whose designated direction is opposite to its travel.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On the same divided highway, a car drives along the roadway in its designated direction.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives on an undivided two-way highway: no median or dividing section lies on the way.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along one roadway of a divided highway; the source declares st.lane_direction absent, so whether it travels against the roadway's direction is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car that has turned left through a median opening crosses the opposite roadway at a right angle to its designated direction to reach a side street.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: Ground-truth simulator kinematics sampled at 20 Hz and the speed noise of typical odometry

param_proposals.name: p.opposed_direction_cosine
param_proposals.convention: Direction tolerance: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between a velocity and a carrier's designated direction that counts as travel against it; motion at a smaller angle, crossing included, does not.
param_proposals.source: Wrong-way detection conventions in trajectory analysis and heading tolerance of ground-truth simulation

segmentation.text: Every vehicle driven
upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and
must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection
established by a public authority

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed as one atom; 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading below).

A divided highway is 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section' (DEF-NRS-484A-070): an st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which (st.on_way) an st.median_or_divider lies ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'), its parts being st.roadway regions ('separate roadways of a divided highway are separate'). 'upon' is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a roadway or dividing section lying on that highway; st.highway's exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' is respected: the roadway is read as the part of the way it is.

'any dividing space, barrier or section' is the st.median_or_divider, 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways', lying on the divided highway; 'driven over, across or within' it is x's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies) at any observation: on it, crossing it or standing within it. On a divided highway a left, semicircular or U-turn made off an opening, crossover or intersection shows in its outcome: a left turn from a roadway crosses the dividing section on its left (st.median_or_divider, rel.occupies), and a semicircular or U-turn, 'the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction' (DEF-NRS-484B-077), either crosses it or leaves the vehicle proceeding against the designated direction (st.lane_direction) of the roadway it occupies: drv.motion.against_carrier_direction(x, r), from kin.velocity and kin.speed. The concept is 'Not a stand-in for' the heading opposing the carrier, so a vehicle backing is read by its motion.

st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': 'an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space' is the dividing-section region carrying that attribute, and 'through' it is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) such a region.

'a crossover' is the same opening of the dividing section (st.median_or_divider, 'opening attribute where a crossover exists'); 'intersection' is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet', which with DEF-NRS-484A-105 (2) makes 'every crossing of each roadway of such divided highway by an intersecting highway ... a separate intersection'. 'at' is x's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) such an opening or intersection.

'established by a public authority' (DEF-NRS-484A-195, 'the Department of Transportation or the local authority having jurisdiction') is the legal status of the opening, crossover or intersection; its presence on the road (an st.median_or_divider region with the opening attribute, an st.intersection) is the evidence of that status (status reading below).

applicability: x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) and occupies (rel.occupies) an st.roadway or st.median_or_divider region lying on (st.on_way) an st.highway region h on which some st.median_or_divider region lies.
obligation: Re-binding h with the same selection: at the observation, unless x occupies an st.median_or_divider region lying on h that carries the opening attribute, or occupies an st.intersection region lying on h, neither (a) x occupies an st.median_or_divider region lying on h, nor (b) x occupies an st.roadway region r lying on h and moves against its designated direction: drv.motion.against_carrier_direction(x, r) with speed_floor p.speed_resolution and opposed_cosine p.opposed_direction_cosine.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the highway is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever controls it.

The left, semicircular and U-turns are read through their outcome on the divided highway, not as manoeuvres recognized from the heading: crossing the dividing section, or proceeding against the designated direction of the roadway occupied ('so as to proceed in the opposite direction'); a left turn that leaves the roadway on its left without touching the dividing section is not read, and a vehicle travelling against a roadway's direction without having turned is judged here too.
'established by a public authority' is read through the presence of the opening, crossover or intersection on the road: the feature's presence is the evidence of its establishment.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a highway divided by a grass median, a car drives across the median at a place where the median region carries no opening and no intersection lies.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On the same divided highway, a car turns left across the median through a median region that carries the opening attribute and then drives in the designated direction of the opposite roadway.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car makes a U-turn on an undivided two-way highway: no median or dividing section lies on the way.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car drives near the median of a divided highway; the source declares rel.occupies absent, so whether it is on the median, an opening or a roadway is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On a wide roadway of a divided highway, away from any opening and intersection, a car makes a U-turn without touching the median and drives on against the roadway's designated direction.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car makes a U-turn inside an intersection of the divided highway and leaves on the opposite roadway in its designated direction.

param_proposals.name: p.speed_resolution
param_proposals.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
param_proposals.source: Ground-truth simulator kinematics sampled at 20 Hz and the speed noise of typical odometry

param_proposals.name: p.opposed_direction_cosine
param_proposals.convention: Direction tolerance: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between a velocity and a carrier's designated direction that counts as travel against it; motion at a smaller angle, crossing included, does not.
param_proposals.source: Wrong-way detection conventions in trajectory analysis and heading tolerance of ground-truth simulation

contract: A road user is in motion at the observation: its speed exceeds speed_floor. The floor names only the source's speed resolution, below which a reading counts as no motion; speed (kin.speed) is in m/s. The concept says nothing of the direction of motion relative to the body or to the road, of a manoeuvre, or of who or what controls the motion. Not denoted: a halt held for a duration, travel along a particular carrier, or a road user being driven by a person.

params.name: speed_floor
params.meaning: the source's speed resolution: a speed at or below it counts as no motion

elements.justification: kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; it carries no direction, which the contract does not state.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car travels along a lane at ordinary urban speed, far above the floor.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car stands at a stop line with zero speed.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares kin.speed absent.

contract: A road user moves backwards relative to its own body at the observation: the component of its velocity along its heading is below minus speed_floor. Velocity (kin.velocity) is in m/s in the world frame and heading (kin.heading) is read normalised; speed_floor is the source's speed resolution, so a standing or barely creeping body is not reversing. It is read from kinematics only, never from the gear selected: a vehicle in reverse gear that rolls forward is not reversing, and one in a forward gear that rolls backwards is. Not denoted: a turn, the path followed, or the place the road user is in.

params.name: speed_floor
params.meaning: the source's speed resolution: a rearward velocity component at or below it counts as no backward motion

elements.span: the component of its velocity along its heading is below minus speed_floor
elements.justification: kin.velocity is the 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame) and kin.heading the 'direction the body points', read normalised; their dot product is the velocity component along the body axis. kin.gear is 'Not a stand-in for: the direction of motion' and is not read.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car moves backwards out of a parking bay, its velocity opposite to its heading.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car drives forward along a lane.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car moves near a parking bay; the source declares kin.heading absent.

contract: A road user's heading is changing at the observation: the absolute value of its yaw rate exceeds yaw_floor. Yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) is in deg/s, left positive, and either hand counts; yaw_floor is the source's yaw-rate resolution. Not denoted: a turn at a junction, a lane change, or the curvature of the road: a road user yaws wherever its path bends, and one running straight does not.

params.name: yaw_floor
params.meaning: the source's yaw-rate resolution: an absolute yaw rate at or below it counts as no heading change

elements.span: the absolute value of its yaw rate exceeds yaw_floor
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left'; it is 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature', and the concept reads the body's own heading change, not the road's shape.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car swings its heading while backing around a curb, its yaw rate well above the floor.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along a straight lane with zero yaw rate.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares kin.yaw_rate absent.

contract: A road user moves clockwise about a structure region's reference point at the observation, viewed from above in the world frame, whose positive sense of rotation is counter-clockwise (the sense in which a yaw rate is positive). It holds where the road user is moving (drv.motion.moving with speed_floor) and the cross product of the vector from the region's reference point to the road user's reference point with the road user's velocity is negative and larger in magnitude than sine_tolerance times the product of that vector's length and the road user's speed, compared as squares: the sine of the angle from that radius vector to the velocity is below minus sine_tolerance. The region's reference point is read from st.region_geometry, the road user's from kin.position, its velocity from kin.velocity and its speed from kin.speed, in m and m/s. Motion toward or away from the reference point, within the tolerance, is neither sense. Not denoted: travel against a carrier's designated direction, a change of the road user's heading, or the road user being inside the region: the caller states occupancy.

params.name: speed_floor
params.meaning: the source's speed resolution: a road user at or below it has no sense of motion

params.name: sine_tolerance
params.meaning: the sine of the largest angle off the radial line within which motion counts as neither sense of rotation

elements.span: the road user is moving (drv.motion.moving with speed_floor)
elements.justification: drv.motion.moving, co-proposed: speed above the source's resolution.

elements.span: The region's reference point is read from st.region_geometry, the road user's from kin.position, its velocity from kin.velocity and its speed from kin.speed
elements.justification: st.region_geometry gives 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame'; kin.position is the 'position of the body's reference point' (m, world frame); kin.velocity the 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame); kin.speed the 'magnitude of velocity'. The region's distance (st.region_geometry's ground distance) is not read: the radius runs from reference point to reference point.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car on the circulatory roadway drives around the central island clockwise, its velocity tangential to the radius from the roundabout's reference point.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car on the circulatory roadway drives around the central island counter-clockwise.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car moves on the circulatory roadway; the source declares kin.velocity absent.

contract: A road user moves against the designated direction of a travel carrier at the observation. It holds where the road user is moving (drv.motion.moving with speed_floor) and the component of its velocity along the carrier's designated direction is below minus opposed_cosine times its speed: the angle between its velocity and that direction is wider than the angle whose cosine is minus opposed_cosine. Velocity (kin.velocity) and speed (kin.speed) are in m/s in the world frame; the designated direction (st.lane_direction) is read normalised and is unknown where the carrier carries none. Crossing the carrier, or any motion at a smaller angle to the designated direction than that, is not against it. Not denoted: the road user's heading opposing the carrier (a body backing along a lane faces against it but moves with it), two road users being oncoming, or the road user being on the carrier: the caller states occupancy.

params.name: speed_floor
params.meaning: the source's speed resolution: a road user at or below it has no direction of travel

params.name: opposed_cosine
params.meaning: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between the velocity and the designated direction that counts as against it

elements.span: the road user is moving (drv.motion.moving with speed_floor)
elements.justification: drv.motion.moving, co-proposed: speed above the source's resolution.

elements.span: Velocity (kin.velocity) and speed (kin.speed) are in m/s in the world frame
elements.justification: kin.velocity is the 'velocity vector' (m/s, world frame) and kin.speed its magnitude; the velocity, not kin.heading, is read, so a backing body is judged by its motion.

elements.span: the designated direction (st.lane_direction) is read normalised and is unknown where the carrier carries none
elements.justification: st.lane_direction is the 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane, ... or a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder', read normalised; 'a place no carrier covers has none (unknown)'.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along a one-way roadway opposite to its designated direction.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along the same roadway in its designated direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car drives along a roadway; the source declares st.lane_direction absent.

contract: Road user x is passing road user y on y's right at the observation: the side-by-side phase of an overtaking. It holds where their headings are aligned (rel.same_direction, with aligned_cosine as the relation's tolerance), their bodies overlap along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive), y lies on x's left (the lateral component of rel.bearing of y from x, in x's frame), and x's speed exceeds y's (kin.speed, m/s) by more than speed_margin, the speed resolution below which the two count as keeping pace. Not denoted: the approach from behind or the return ahead of y, where either body is on the road, a lane change, contact, or the clearance between the bodies.

params.name: aligned_cosine
params.meaning: the cosine of the largest angle between the two headings that counts as aligned

params.name: speed_margin
params.meaning: the speed resolution of a speed difference: an excess at or below it counts as keeping pace

elements.span: their headings are aligned (rel.same_direction, with aligned_cosine as the relation's tolerance)
elements.justification: rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance'.

elements.span: their bodies overlap along x's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap positive)
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)'; it is 'neither a contact nor a distance between the bodies', and neither is read from it.

elements.span: y lies on x's left (the lateral component of rel.bearing of y from x, in x's frame)
elements.justification: rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of", ...)'.

elements.span: x's speed exceeds y's (kin.speed, m/s) by more than speed_margin
elements.justification: kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity', m/s, read for both road users.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x drives on the shoulder alongside a slower y in the rightmost lane, y on x's left, the bodies side by side, x gaining.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x follows y in the same lane, its body wholly behind y's.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x and y are side by side and x is faster; the source declares rel.bearing absent.

contract: The signed heading change of road user x since its footprint last began to overlap region r, in degrees, left positive: zero at the observation at which the overlap began, integrated from x's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) with step as the sampling step bound, not ended by x leaving r and restarted only by its next entry into r. Unknown where that entry is not observed with the overlap known at every observation since, where two consecutive observations since lie further apart than step, or where a yaw rate since the entry is missing. Not denoted: a turn manoeuvre by itself (a caller compares the change with its own bound, and a bend of the way inside the region changes it too), or the heading change over a fixed window.

params.name: step
params.meaning: the sampling step bound of the integration: the largest interval between consecutive observations it integrates across

elements.span: its footprint last began to overlap region r
elements.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; its latest rise is the entry the change is counted from.

elements.span: integrated from x's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) with step as the sampling step bound
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left'; integrated by the formula language's heading-since construct, whose step bound is this parameter.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: x enters an intersection and turns a quarter turn to the right before leaving; the value at the exit lies in the band about minus a right angle that the instance's bounds state.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: x drives straight through the intersection; the value at the exit stays near zero, outside that band.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: x enters and leaves the intersection; the source declares kin.yaw_rate absent.
